scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The portal depends on others
scenes.caption: Kabir evaluates a fictional event-service supplier and a payment integration. The supplier can publish a programme without downloading registrations. The team also depends on updates, private secrets and a recovery route that must work during an outage.
scenes.dialogue: Which dependency can affect the whole service?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: A constrained budget
scenes.caption: The exercise gives the team six budget units. Three targeted controls cost two units each: least-privilege supplier access, private managed secrets with rotation, and independent tested recovery. Decorative assurance badges cannot replace these requirements.
scenes.dialogue: Use the stated needs to defend the spend.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Minimum access and exit
scenes.caption: Limit purpose, scope, duration and onward sharing. Name the owner who revokes access when work ends. Keep a trusted update route and avoid putting integration secrets in the client or a group chat. Test recovery independently of the failed supplier.
scenes.dialogue: A supplier agreement needs an exit as well as an entry.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose the supplier access
scenes.caption: The supplier needs to publish the programme. Should it receive the full registration export, a shared organiser account, or only programme-publishing access that expires after the task?

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: An owned dependency decision
scenes.caption: The team funds the required controls within the supplied budget and records what remains outside it. A minimum-access agreement and independent recovery test reduce exposure, but cannot promise uninterrupted service or eliminate supplier failure.
scenes.dialogue: Keep the remaining dependency risk explicit.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the dependency lab
scenes.caption: Allocate the exercise budget, build the minimum-access agreement and respond to a supplier outage. Explain both the selected safeguards and the remaining risk; no real supplier is being rated.
scenes.dialogue: Decide from the task and evidence, not a badge.
